subject: english-literature
topicDisplay: Poetry Anthology: Power and Conflict / Love and Relationships
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Who wrote the poem 'Ozymandias' in the Power and Conflict cluster?
questions.explain: 'Ozymandias' is a sonnet by Percy Bysshe Shelley describing a ruined statue in the desert.

questions.q: 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' by Tennyson describes a disastrous cavalry charge during which war?
questions.explain: The poem depicts the charge at the Battle of Balaclava in the Crimean War (1854).

questions.q: Which First World War poet wrote 'Exposure', about soldiers dying in the freezing cold?
questions.explain: Wilfred Owen wrote 'Exposure', focusing on the deadly weather rather than enemy fire.

questions.q: 'Checking Out Me History', which uses phonetic non-standard spelling to explore identity, was written by:
questions.explain: John Agard wrote 'Checking Out Me History', protesting a curriculum that omitted black history.

questions.q: Which Power and Conflict poem is a dramatic monologue spoken by the Duke of Ferrara?
questions.explain: Robert Browning's 'My Last Duchess' is narrated by a controlling Duke describing a portrait of his late wife.

questions.q: The refrain 'But nothing happens' in Owen's 'Exposure' mainly emphasises:
options: The deadly monotony and futility of waiting in the cold
The soldiers' excitement before an attack
The comfort of the soldiers' surroundings
questions.explain: The repeated line stresses the numbing, hopeless stasis in which the men slowly die of exposure.

questions.q: In 'Ozymandias', the ruined statue half-sunk in the sand primarily symbolises:
options: The impermanence of human power and pride
The beauty of the natural desert
questions.explain: The 'colossal wreck' shows that even a boastful tyrant's power is eventually erased by time.

questions.q: Blake's phrase 'mind-forg'd manacles' in 'London' suggests that people's suffering is:
options: Partly created by imposed and internalised ways of thinking
questions.explain: The metaphor implies the Londoners are trapped by mental and social constraints, not just physical chains.

questions.q: In Garland's 'Kamikaze', the pilot's decision to turn back and not complete his mission results in:
options: Him being shunned and treated as though he were dead
Him being celebrated as a hero
A promotion in the air force
A joyful reunion with his commanders
questions.explain: On returning home the pilot is rejected by his family and community, a living dishonour worse than death.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Before You Were Mine', a poem addressed to the poet's mother?
questions.explain: Carol Ann Duffy imagines her mother's carefree life before the speaker was born.

questions.q: 'Sonnet 29 – I think of thee' in the Love and Relationships cluster was written by:
questions.explain: Elizabeth Barrett Browning's sonnet uses an extended plant-and-tree metaphor for overwhelming love.

questions.q: In Browning's 'Porphyria's Lover', the speaker kills Porphyria by:
options: Strangling her with her own hair
questions.explain: The obsessive speaker winds her long yellow hair around her throat to preserve the moment forever.

questions.q: Which Love and Relationships poem uses an extended metaphor of climbing a mountain to describe a relative?
questions.explain: Andrew Waterhouse's 'Climbing My Grandfather' treats the grandfather's body as a mountain the speaker scales.

questions.q: Armitage's 'Mother, any distance' uses the metaphor of a tape measure mainly to explore:
options: A child's growing independence from a parent
The measuring of a new house for sale
A journey across a foreign country
questions.explain: The unreeling tape captures the tension between the mother holding on and the child moving away.

questions.q: The grey imagery and 'God-curst sun' in Hardy's 'Neutral Tones' create an overall tone of:
questions.explain: The bleak, colourless setting mirrors the speaker's cynicism after a relationship's failure.

questions.q: In Causley's 'Eden Rock', the closing line 'I had not thought that it would be like this' most suggests:
options: A gentle realisation about death and reunion with his parents
Confusion about directions on a walk
questions.explain: The idealised memory of his parents becomes an image of a peaceful crossing into death.

questions.q: In the AQA anthology exam, the poetry comparison question requires you to compare the named printed poem with:
options: Another poem you choose from the same cluster
An unseen poem printed beside it
Any poem from a different cluster
A poem written by the same poet only
questions.explain: You compare the given poem to one other poem you select from the same anthology cluster.

questions.q: A student wants to compare how poets present the lasting psychological effects of conflict. The best pairing is:
questions.explain: Both poems focus on trauma and guilt experienced after witnessing violence, not the fighting itself.

questions.q: To compare how poets present a parent-child relationship, the strongest pairing from the Love and Relationships cluster is:
options: 'When We Two Parted' and 'The Farmer's Bride'
questions.explain: 'Follower' and 'Walking Away' both explore the shifting bond and distance between a parent and child.

questions.q: To explore how human power is temporary, 'Ozymandias' could best be compared with which Power and Conflict poem?
questions.explain: Both 'Ozymandias' and 'Tissue' present the fragility and impermanence of human control and power.
